thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: elevated 5xx/error rates in ap-south-1 edge gateway detected at 2026-05-14T10:00:00Z. Alerts fired: gateway_5xx_rate, egress_conn_exhaustion, high_syn_backlog. Affected surface: hosted API (/v1/generate), embeddings traffic; approx ~30% error rate in AP region. Runbook: https://go.runbooks/redwood/egress-nat-surge

Caroline: ack — Caroline (oncall) here. I'm triaging. Any immediate config changes or deploys in the last 15m? What's the blast radius (customers / routes)?

Alice: pulling logs + dashboards now. Looks like an egress NAT connection pool saturation on ap-south-1 (lots of SYN retries, TIME_WAIT accumulation). Upstream model workers are returning 502/504 because gateway can't establish outbound connections. Snippet from gateway logs:
```
[2026-05-14T10:00:05Z] gateway-az1 - upstream conn reset to mlworker-3: i/o timeout
[2026-05-14T10:00:06Z] gateway-az1 - upstream 502 from model-proxy-12
[2026-05-14T10:00:06Z] gateway-az1 - connpool exhausted, dropping request
```
Also seeing RTT spike to third-party CDN (cdn-xyz) used for model weights: 120ms -> 850ms, coincident with the spike.

Bob: runtime-engineer here. Model workers show normal CPU/GPU usage, KV cache hitrate steady. This smells like network/egress. We can avoid loading ap-south egress by steering new requests to eu-west-1/2 temporarily for non-local latency-sensitive traffic. Can also enable a lower-latency fallback model variant for non-SLAs to reduce backend connections.

Dave: netops — prepping route steer now. Plan: incremental weight shift to eu-west-1. Also requesting extra NAT capacity from cloud provider. Commands I'll run (dry-run first):
```
# change route weights (rosterctl is our control plane CLI)
rosterctl update-route --route inference-public --region ap-south-1 --weights "ap-south-1:40,eu-west-1:60"
# provision an additional NAT gateway / enlarge pool
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-0abc123 --allocation-id eipalloc-0abc123
```

Caroline: doing a canary shift 10% to eu-west-1 now. Will watch errors and tail latency.

DeployBot: Canary change applied by @Caroline — route inference-public weights changed: ap-south-1=90 eu-west-1=10 (:white_check_mark:)

Alice: telemetry — canary shows 50% lower 5xx for the subset of requests routed to eu-west-1. Ap-south-1 still high for remaining traffic but trending down.

Bob: enabling fallback policy to quantized model variant for best-effort requests to reduce connection pressure (non-critical batch requests):
```
{"policy":"fallback_to_quantized","targets":["/v1/generate"],"threshold":0.05}
```
This should reduce backend connection churn by decreasing per-request processing time.

Erin: support update — Impact summary for status page / customers:
- Scope: Elevated timeouts (504) and 5xx for requests originating in AP region (ap-south-1).
- Start time: ~2026-05-14T10:00:00Z
- User impact: ~12% of AP region requests affected; top customers in AP see increased error rates.
Draft blurb: "We are investigating elevated timeouts in ap-south-1. Traffic is being temporarily routed to other regions while we mitigate. No data loss reported." Approve to post? cc @Frank

Frank: approved. Add note: "No data loss. We're working to restore normal routing. Expect intermittent higher latency for AP customers while traffic is redirected." Send it.

Caroline: posted status update at 2026-05-14T10:06:00Z — public status: "Investigating; traffic being shifted." (link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1765000000)

Mike: (customer) We're seeing timeouts from Singapore office — any ETA?

Erin: replied to Mike privately with targeted mitigation steps and offered alternate endpoint in eu-west. Sent targeted emails to top 5 AP customers.

Alice: metrics at 10:12 UTC: overall 5xx rate for ap-south reduced from 30% -> 3.5% after weight shift + fallback enable. SYN backlog still above threshold but trending down. Suggest keep steering at 60% to eu-west until NAT capacity confirmed.

Dave: cloud provider support ticket opened (ticket #CP-28947). Provider acknowledges a partial network maintenance window affecting NAT throughput for ap-south during 09:58-10:15 UTC. They've put a priority ticket to provision extra NAT capacity.

Caroline: next actions / owners:
- Alice + Dave: follow up with cloud provider for root cause + extra capacity (owner: Dave)
- Alice: create postmortem draft and add runbook improvements (autoscale NAT, better SYN/wait metrics)
- Bob: evaluate edge backpressure so gateway drops early instead of building SYN backlog (owner: Bob)
- Erin: customer comms and incident update cadence (owner: Erin)

Caroline: I'll keep the incident channel open for 1 hour and plan handoff at 11:15 UTC if mitigated. Oncall notes will be added to the runbook.

Alice: 2026-05-14T10:22:00Z — confirmed 5xx returned to baseline (~1.2%). Rolling down steering to ap-south-1=75 eu-west-1=25 to verify stability.

DeployBot: Route weights updated by @Alice — ap-south-1=75 eu-west-1=25 (:white_check_mark:)

Alice: Observed stability for 10m. Closing paging; marking incident mitigated. Will kick off followup postmortem with timeline + action items. (reacted :thumbsup:)

Caroline: 10:35 UTC — creating postmortem draft and assigning owners. Thanks team. Closing this thread and moving to postmortem channel.

-- End of thread --
